reader.requirement: At --std 85 (the 1989 amendment) the compiler must accept FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE ( argument-1 ) with exactly one integer argument and refuse every other shape (no FUNCTION word, no parentheses, zero or two arguments, the 2002 empty list and ALL forms), returning the number of days after 1600-12-31.

edition-consulted.switches: NumericFunctionIdentifierOperand2002: MOVE FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(D) refused at 85

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the format (two_args.cob is refused identically at --std 2023); placement outside an arithmetic expression and the empty list differ.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers two arguments; not exercised: no parentheses, the empty list, legal values, non-integer arguments, ALL.

reader.notes: The same catalog-driven arity path as INTEGER; every value checked by hand against the 400-year Gregorian cycle (146097 days).

refuter.evidence: Read §1989:A.2.16 (one integer argument YYYYMMDD), §1989:A.2.2 AR4 (an arithmetic expression that always results in an integer) and §1989:A.2.3 (a numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required). Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-09/c6: numeric-function arguments NUMVAL and SQRT (numval_arg, sqrt_arg) -> COBOL1627; DD / 2 (div_arg), D ** -1 (negexp_arg), D ** E with signed E (varexp_arg), a PIC 9(8)V9 item (ws_nonint_x) -> COBOL1627; integer forms FUNCTION INTEGER(X), D * 1, D ** 1 (int_fn_arg, mul_arg, exp_arg) -> 146097; difference of two INTEGER-OF-DATE in COMPUTE (int_of_day_ok) -> 146096. Each was the same at --std 2023. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.16.3 AR1; OK §1989:A.2.2 (in AR4); OK §1989:A.2.3 (in GR2).
